title: Breakfast Enchiladas for the Crew
subtitle: Rolled tortillas stuffed with eggs and chorizo under green chili sauce.
description: A hotel-pan bake of flour tortillas rolled tight with scrambled eggs, chorizo, and cheese, then smothered in verde sauce and baked until bubbling. Cuts into clean portions for a crew that wants something bolder than a standard egg bake.

ingredients.name: sour cream
ingredients.notes: whisked into half the sauce for creaminess

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Breakfast Enchiladas for the Crew in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Eggs. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 375°F. Grease a deep 9x13 pan or two smaller hotel pans. Warm tortillas in a dry skillet or wrapped in foil so they roll without tearing. Allow 10–15 minutes for mise en place before heat goes on. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Cook the filling
steps.instruction: Brown chorizo in a large skillet, drain fat, then add soft-scrambled eggs and half the Jack cheese. Mix gently—the eggs should stay fluffy, not mashed. Target 165°F at the thickest part before moving to the next batch. Plan about 15 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Roll the enchiladas
steps.instruction: Spread a thin layer of sauce in the pan. Fill each tortilla with a generous scoop of filling, roll tight, and place seam-side down in a snug single layer. Plan about 12 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Sauce and cheese
steps.instruction: Pour remaining sauce evenly over the rolls. Top with remaining Jack and cotija. Cover with foil for the first half of baking to keep tortillas soft. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Bake and rest
steps.instruction: Bake covered 20 minutes, uncover, and bake 10 more until sauce bubbles at the edges. Rest 10 minutes before cutting into portions so slices hold on the plate. Bake until the center reaches a safe internal temp (165°F) and edges look set — use a thermometer at the thickest point. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

stationWorkflow: Set up a rolling station with warm tortillas, filling bowl, and sauced pan ready before scrambling eggs.
One cook rolls while another manages sauce and oven timing—don't let rolled enchiladas sit dry on the counter.
Garnish with cilantro and lime at the line; hold extra sauce warm for second passes.
cleanupNotes: Soak the chorizo skillet immediately with hot water and a drop of dish soap to cut grease before it sets.
Scrape baked-on cheese from the 9x13 while still warm using a plastic scraper, not a metal blade on glass.
leftovers: Portion enchiladas into containers with extra sauce on top; reheat covered at 325°F until steaming in the center.
Chop leftovers into a breakfast burrito filling with scrambled eggs and hot sauce for handheld service.
